title: Answer: no account of physical time, which enters as the reach of a cognitive light cone

statements.text: Basal cognition takes no position on what time is in physics. Time enters as one axis of a self's cognitive light cone: the most distant events, in time and in space, that a system can measure and tries to regulate. Below the present are past events it may remember, above it future events it may anticipate, and a larger self is one whose goals reach further in both. Nervous systems add control of events in time, and brains add memory and planning of what is not happening now.
statements.scope: the computational boundary of a self (2019) and the paper on navigating arbitrary spaces (2022)

sources.quote: is the most distant (in time and space) set of events that this system can measure and attempts to regulate in its goal-directed activity.
The vertical axis is time. Values below the individual's Now are past events, of which it may have a memory extending some duration in the past
The control of movement via nervous systems is largely about events in time.
